title: Smoothness descends along arbitrary qcqs affine-transition limits
statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty directed set and $(S_i)_{i\in I}$ an inverse system of schemes with affine transition morphisms [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] [pqf-def-affine-morphism], and let $S=\varprojlim_iS_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. Fix $i_0\in I$ and assume $S_{i_0}$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Fix quasi-compact quasi-separated $S_{i_0}$-schemes $X_{i_0},Y_{i_0}$, and an $S_{i_0}$-morphism $f_{i_0}:X_{i_0}\to Y_{i_0}$ locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Write $f_i$ and $f$ for its base changes to $S_i$ and $S$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. If $f$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], there is $i\geq i_0$ such that $f_j$ is smooth for every $j\geq i$. No Noetherian hypothesis is imposed on the stages.

source.place: Tag 0C0C, label lemma-descend-smooth, in Situation situation-descent-property; persistence by base change of smooth morphisms

proof.text: Base change the original diagram along the structure map Y₀ → S₀ and restrict its index to Over i₀. The diagram has terms Y₀ ×_{S₀} S_j and limit Y₀ ×_{S₀} S. This follows directly by the fibre-product universal property and initiality of Over i₀. Its transitions are affine by base change. The identity-stage term is canonically isomorphic to Y₀, so it is compact and quasi-separated. Lift f₀ to this term and identify its limit pullback with the stated base change of f₀ by pullback pasting. In Lean these are baseChangeDiagram, isLimitBaseChangeCone, and the private helper exists_smooth_over_pullback.

source.place: Tag 0C0C, label lemma-descend-smooth, affine-local reduction; Situation 081D

proof.text: For the resulting finite-presentation map p : P → X_i, cover the compact quasi-separated target X_i by finitely many affine opens B_a. Since P is compact and X_i is quasi-separated, p is quasi-compact; hence the inverse image of each B_a is compact. Cover each inverse image by finitely many affine opens and bind these covers to a finite source cover U. The restriction a : U_k → B_a is locally of finite presentation by cancellation of the open immersion B_a → X_i. Restrict limit smoothness by source open immersion and cancel the target open immersion, using the canonical iterated-pullback comparison. No Noetherian hypothesis and no affine-intersection hypothesis is used.

source.place: Tag 0C0C, label lemma-descend-smooth, affine-local reduction; Situation 081D

proof.text: Base change the system to B_a. Its terms are affine because its projections to the affine scheme B_a are base changes of affine transition maps. Its limit is the pullback to B_a by the same universal property. Apply the already proved Scheme.exists_smooth_stage_of_affine_diagram to a : U_k → B_a, its finite-presentation instance, and the smooth limit pullback. This theorem translates global sections to a filtered colimit and applies the approved fixed-map ring pushout descent theorem; it is exactly steps 3–4 of the original plan packaged in a reusable proved declaration. It gives a smooth stage for each chart.

source.place: Tag 0C0C, label lemma-descend-smooth, affine-local reduction; Situation 081D

proof.text: Choose a common refinement of the finitely many chart stages in Over i. Pullback pasting and smooth base-change stability transport each chart to that refinement. The pulled-back U_k cover its source. Compose each restricted chart map with the target open inclusion and use source locality to obtain smoothness of the full pullback of p. IsCofiltered.inf_objs_exists also applies to the empty finite set, so this proves the empty-source case as well. This is the private helper descend_smooth_to_stage.

source.place: Tag 0C0C, label lemma-descend-smooth, affine-local reduction; Situation 081D

proof.text: For any still later object, the pullback of p is the further base change of the smooth stage. The iterated-pullback isomorphism preserves its projection, so smoothness persists. Compare this pullback with the original Over.pullback map by the unique isomorphism between two pullback squares for f₀.left over Y₀; the equations on both projections prove that the morphisms correspond. Finally take opposite indices: an arrow op i → op i₀ is i₀ ≤ i, and the arrow for i ≤ j gives exactly the composite in the unchanged conclusion.

source.place: Tag 0C0C, label lemma-descend-smooth, affine-local reduction; Situation 081D
